title: Benchmark-depth premium analysis — owner-verified facts
summary: The 09/09 premium benchmark brief is the canonical one-link output: 18 ordered sections, benchmark-scale depth, exact source receipts, claims/context, Creator-DNA remake directions, Vault entry and Markdown/PDF export. Subscriber enrichment is now tied to the exact analyzed video's YouTube owner block, and the Blake production gate only passes within 10% of the ~6.19K benchmark count.
discord_changes: 18-SCREEN PREMIUM: Strip → Export follows the 09/09 benchmark order at Blake-analysis depth.
OWNER-VERIFIED SUBS: subscriber facts are bound to the exact analyzed video; Blake must land within ±10% of ~6.19K.
ENDGAME OUTPUT: claims + channel context + Creator DNA finish in 2–3 executable remake directions with measurement plans.
changes: Locked the 18-section order from the Analyse One Link brief: Strip, Summary, Key Takeaways, Hook, Re-hooks, Payoffs, Most Replayed, Structure Map, Visuals, Motion Graphics, Audio, Packaging, Numbers Table, Claims Ledger, Channel Context, Make It Yours, Vault Entry and Export.
Kept the Endgame promise intact: replace watching the source, expose the evidence under each conclusion, and finish with the user's own video blueprint rather than a generic analytics dump.
Matched the Blake Ryan benchmark's useful depth with per-section QA targets instead of padding every section to arbitrary length.
Added the benchmark-style short version: what the video is, how it is built, how it is doing, what appears to matter and what is worth taking.
Expanded the first 60 seconds into line-by-line hook analysis and retained chronological re-hook/payoff receipts across the full runtime.
Added the dedicated Structure Map, Numbers Table, Claims Ledger and Channel Context surfaces required by the 09/09 brief.
Kept Most Replayed, storyboard/frame, motion and audio claims evidence-bounded; unavailable public evidence stays unavailable instead of being fabricated.
Added current title-surface evidence without falsely asserting an A/B test when only public discrepancies are visible.
Fixed the Title Surface Check race so Packaging is complete immediately and slower channel enrichment no longer blocks it.
Replaced loose subscriber scraping with an exact analyzed-video owner-renderer lookup, matched to the source channel ID before accepting subscriberCountText.
Kept channel-page and operational About data only as secondary fallbacks; unknown subscriber evidence remains unknown rather than zero.
Strengthened the deployed Blake browser proof from merely nonzero to ±10% of the 6,190 benchmark subscriber count, so unrelated shelf/card counts cannot pass.
The production proof still requires all 18 sections, premium depth floors, claims/context/remake/export coverage, transcript evidence, title-surface evidence, mobile containment and zero page errors.
Preserved Group Analysis, Watchtower, source taxonomy, account-backed Creator DNA and the compounding Vault.
known_limitations: External factual verification across the open web is not fabricated in zero-credit mode. Claims that only exist in the source remain THEIR CLAIM unless public evidence or arithmetic can verify or contradict them.
Public search validation is a sample, not a census, and YouTube can expose different or incomplete surfaces over time.
YouTube may not expose storyboards, direct media, comments, subscribers or Most Replayed on every request. Missing evidence stays explicitly unavailable.
Storyboard frames are seek-bar samples rather than every encoded video frame; exact cut/zoom/audio claims require reliable media access or a supported on-device multimodal model.
On-device multimodal model support depends on browser/device availability and is explicit opt-in. The 18-section source-evidence report still runs without it.
why_it_matters: The product is now judged against the hand-built premium benchmark, not against whether a dashboard rendered. It has to save the watch/research time, survive factual cross-checks, and leave the creator with a better original video to make.
